\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Restriction Compose}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.RestrictionCompose
\section{Overview}

This module shows that Bernoulli random restrictions compose: applying a
Bernoulli($p$) restriction and then a Bernoulli($q$) restriction on the remaining
free variables yields the same distribution as a single Bernoulli($pq$) restriction.
It introduces the composition of two restrictions and the per-variable weight, and
builds up through factorization and fiber-weight identities to the main composition
equality and its probabilistic inequality corollary.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Composition of two restrictions]
\lean{LMN.composeRestr}
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004}
\label{LMN.composeRestr}
\leanok
\uses{SwitchingLemma2.Restriction}
Given two restrictions $\rho_1, \rho_2$ on $n$ variables, their composition is the
restriction that on each coordinate $i$ uses the value fixed by $\rho_1$ if there is
one, and otherwise the value given by $\rho_2$. This models applying $\rho_1$ first
and then $\rho_2$ on the variables left free by $\rho_1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Per-variable Bernoulli weight]
\lean{LMN.varWeight}
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{pdf-fc447f326910-p006-b003}
\label{LMN.varWeight}
\leanok
For a parameter $p \in \bbr$, the per-variable weight assigns $p$ to a free
coordinate (value \texttt{none}) and $(1-p)/2$ to a fixed coordinate (value
\texttt{some\_}), matching the marginal of the Bernoulli restriction model.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Pointwise criterion for a composed restriction]
\lean{LMN.composeRestr_eq_iff}
\label{LMN.composeRestr_eq_iff}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composeRestr, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\rho_1,\rho_2,\sigma$ be restrictions on $n$ variables, and let $\rho_1 \ast
\rho_2$ denote the composition of $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$, whose value at a coordinate $i$
is the value fixed by $\rho_1$ at $i$ if $\rho_1$ fixes it and otherwise the value
$\rho_2$ assigns at $i$. Then $\rho_1 \ast \rho_2 = \sigma$ if and only if, for every
coordinate $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the value of $\rho_1 \ast \rho_2$ at $i$ equals
$\sigma(i)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The empty restriction as a right identity for composition]
\lean{LMN.composeRestr_id_right}
\label{LMN.composeRestr_id_right}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composeRestr, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables, and let $\varnothing$ denote the empty
restriction that leaves every variable free. Then the composition of $\rho$ with
$\varnothing$, applying $\rho$ first and then $\varnothing$ on the variables $\rho$
leaves free, equals $\rho$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bernoulli restriction weight as a product over coordinates]
\lean{LMN.bernoulliRestrWeight_eq_prod}
\label{LMN.bernoulliRestrWeight_eq_prod}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.varWeight, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction.freeVars, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight}
\difficulty{5}
Let $p$ be a real parameter and let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables, assigning
each coordinate either a fixed Boolean value or leaving it free. Writing $k$ for the
number of free coordinates, the Bernoulli weight of $\rho$ equals the product over all
$n$ coordinates of the per-variable weights:
\[
  p^{k}\left(\tfrac{1-p}{2}\right)^{\,n-k}
  \;=\;
  \prod_{i=1}^{n} w_p\bigl(\rho(i)\bigr),
\]
where each factor $w_p(\rho(i))$ equals $p$ when coordinate $i$ is free and $(1-p)/2$
when it is fixed.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Composition law for per-variable restriction weights]
\lean{LMN.varWeight_compose_sum}
\label{LMN.varWeight_compose_sum}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.varWeight}
\difficulty{3}
Regard each coordinate of a random restriction as being in one of three states: *free*
(written $\ast$) or *fixed* to one of the two Boolean values. For a parameter $p \in
\bbr$, let $w_p$ be the per-variable weight assigning $w_p(\ast) = p$ to the free state
and $(1-p)/2$ to each of the two fixed states, and define the composite $a \circ b$ of
two states to equal $a$ when $a$ is fixed and $b$ when $a$ is free. Then for all $p, q
\in \bbr$ and every state $c$,
\[
  \sum_{a}\sum_{b} w_p(a)\, w_q(b)\, [\,a \circ b = c\,] = w_{pq}(c),
\]
where both sums range over the three states and $[\,\cdot\,]$ equals $1$ when the
enclosed equation holds and $0$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Composition law for Bernoulli restriction weights]
\lean{LMN.compose_fiber_weight_eq}
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004}
\label{LMN.compose_fiber_weight_eq}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.bernoulliRestrWeight_eq_prod, LMN.composeRestr, LMN.varWeight, LMN.varWeight_compose_sum, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight}
\difficulty{6}
Fix parameters $p, q \in \bbr$ and a restriction $\sigma$ on $n$ variables. Summing the
product of the Bernoulli weight of $\rho_1$ at parameter $p$ and the Bernoulli weight of
$\rho_2$ at parameter $q$ over all pairs of restrictions $(\rho_1, \rho_2)$ on $n$
variables whose composition equals $\sigma$ yields the Bernoulli weight of $\sigma$ at
parameter $pq$:
\[
  \sum_{\rho_1}\sum_{\rho_2}
    w_p(\rho_1)\, w_q(\rho_2)\,
    [\,\rho_1 \circ \rho_2 = \sigma\,]
  = w_{pq}(\sigma),
\]
where $w_r(\rho)$ denotes the Bernoulli weight of $\rho$ at parameter $r$, $\rho_1 \circ
\rho_2$ is the restriction that fixes each coordinate to the value given by $\rho_1$
where defined and to that of $\rho_2$ otherwise, and $[\,\cdot\,]$ is the indicator
taking the value $1$ when its condition holds and $0$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Composition law for Bernoulli random restrictions]
\lean{LMN.restriction_compose_eq}
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004}
\label{LMN.restriction_compose_eq}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composeRestr, LMN.compose_fiber_weight_eq, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight}
\difficulty{5}
Fix real parameters $p, q$ with $0 < p \le 1$ and $0 < q \le 1$, and let $E$ be any
decidable predicate on the restrictions of $n$ variables. Write $w_p(\rho)$ for the
Bernoulli weight of a restriction $\rho$, write $\Pr_p[E]$ for the Bernoulli($p$)
probability of $E$, and let $\rho_1 * \rho_2$ denote the composition of $\rho_1$ and
$\rho_2$. Then
\[
\Pr_{pq}[E] \;=\; \sum_{\rho_1} w_p(\rho_1)\,\Pr_q\!\bigl[\,\rho_2 \mapsto E(\rho_1 *
\rho_2)\,\bigr],
\]
where the sum runs over all restrictions $\rho_1$ on the $n$ variables, and the inner
probability is that of the event that $E$ holds of the composition $\rho_1 * \rho_2$ as
$\rho_2$ ranges over a Bernoulli($q$) restriction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Composition inequality for Bernoulli random restrictions]
\lean{LMN.restriction_compose_le}
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004}
\label{LMN.restriction_compose_le}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composeRestr, LMN.restriction_compose_eq, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb_le_one', SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight_nonneg'}
\difficulty{6}
Fix $n$, let $E$ be an event on restrictions of $n$ variables, and let $0 < p \le 1$ and
$0 < q \le 1$ be real parameters. Then the probability that $E$ holds under a
Bernoulli$(pq)$ random restriction is at most the probability, under a Bernoulli$(p)$
random restriction $\rho_1$, that there is some restriction $\rho_2$ for which $E$ holds
of the composition of $\rho_1$ with $\rho_2$:
\[
  \Pr_{\rho \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(pq)}\bigl[E(\rho)\bigr]
  \;\le\;
\Pr_{\rho_1 \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)}\bigl[\,\exists\,\rho_2\ :\ E(\rho_1 \circ
\rho_2)\,\bigr].
\]
\end{theorem}
